DEV-1b227481f869.notes: The documented DataWriteOptions shape (mtime/ctime) is implemented end to end: mtime is validated, applied via fs.utimes in src/main/vault-write.ts's writeVaultFile(), and forwarded through the preload/IPC boundary and Vault.create/Vault.modify. ctime is accepted for shape compatibility but intentionally not applied (see API-MEMBER-4a325cdd6867).

API-5c4c8dad9e1d.notes: src/renderer/vault.ts exports a DataWriteOptions interface matching the documented { ctime?: number; mtime?: number } shape, threaded through Vault.create/Vault.modify, window.geode.write, and the vault-write IPC handler into writeVaultFile().

API-MEMBER-1a702f175420.notes: writeVaultFile()'s validateMtime() rejects non-finite values (throwing before any mkdir/writeFile mutation runs, verified by asserting the target file was never created) and converts a valid ms-since-epoch value to the seconds fs.utimes expects; the applied mtime is observed exactly on disk via fsp.stat, and via the TFile returned by Vault.create/updated by Vault.modify.

API-MEMBER-4a325cdd6867.notes: Node/Electron's fs.utimes can only set atime/mtime, not birthtime, so a caller-requested ctime cannot be applied to a file's actual creation time on any platform this app ships on. writeVaultFile() accepts options.ctime for API shape compatibility and documents this as a deliberate gap rather than a defect; the test observes ctime being accepted without being reflected in the file's real birthtime.

API-101dd09719d8.notes: parsePropertyId splits on the first dot only (so a nested frontmatter path survives) and treats an unrecognised prefix or a bare id as frontmatter shorthand. This is load-bearing beyond typing: a view uses parsePropertyId(id).name to choose the frontmatter key it writes to.

API-5334fc27aa90.notes: Value is the abstract base of the boundary representation handed to views. Every wrapper defers toString/isTruthy to the expression engine's own coercion rules, so the API layer cannot disagree with the engine about what a value means.

DEV-e36b06fc6f8c.notes: Value is the abstract base class of the Bases value hierarchy.

API-MEMBER-905de1975fb1.notes: Value.type is the static discriminator on each concrete subclass.

API-MEMBER-974c62f635ff.notes: toString() delegates to the engine's valueToDisplayString for every arm.

API-MEMBER-8b0761571075.notes: isTruthy() delegates to the engine's isTruthy for every arm.

API-MEMBER-cec918cfe8e9.notes: equals() is type-strict and null-safe in both its instance and static forms.

API-MEMBER-6f15e5e4ecbc.notes: looseEquals() uses the engine's cross-type comparison rules, which relate a link to the file it resolves to.

API-MEMBER-0508e7d1f7e0.notes: renderTo() paints a value into an element: plain text by default, with richer overrides for lists, images, HTML and links. LinkValue emits <a class="internal-link" data-href="...">, which is load-bearing rather than cosmetic because views wire navigation with a delegated on('click', 'a.internal-link') handler that reads data-href. Observed in real Electron: the e2e board's card property values are painted through renderTo.

API-6244c4a8a4b8.notes: The two documented static helpers (isModEvent, isModifier) are implemented. The instance scope-stack methods pushScope/popScope need scope infrastructure Geode does not have and are deliberately absent rather than stubbed, so calling them raises a TypeError instead of silently pretending to bind a keymap.

DEV-3c09e9409b53.notes: isModEvent and isModifier are implemented; pushScope/popScope are absent rather than stubbed.

API-MEMBER-bae88d974fd9.notes: isModEvent returns 'tab' for the platform Mod key or a middle-click, 'split' for Mod+Alt, 'window' for Mod+Alt+Shift, and false otherwise, per the documented rules. The Mod key is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, strictly one or the other, since Ctrl-click on macOS is the context-menu gesture.

DEV-22bec1688869.notes: isModEvent implements the documented tab/split/window/false mapping, including middle-click as 'tab'.

API-MEMBER-41402f88fd45.notes: isModifier reads each named modifier off the event, resolving 'Mod' to the platform key.

API-MEMBER-ab70653f1ffc.notes: The TFile overload plugins actually call, distinct from the adapter path-string form. A card cover image rendered by the real kanban-bases-view plugin is observed reaching a non-zero naturalWidth in Electron, so the URL is loadable rather than merely well-formed. Throws where no filesystem adapter exists (mobile) instead of returning a URL that would render as a permanently broken image.

API-MEMBER-790bb8b3d573.notes: Percent-encodes each path segment rather than escaping only spaces, so a name containing # or ? no longer yields a URL truncated at the fragment or query. Ordinary paths are byte-for-byte unchanged.

API-MEMBER-f7b0709fe093.notes: Accepts the documented PaneType | boolean rather than a bare boolean: getLeaf('tab') previously worked only because a non-empty string is truthy, and 'split' would have silently produced a tab. Partial, not verified: 'window' throws because Geode has no pop-out windows, and the 'split' overload ignores its SplitDirection because Geode's main area only produces side-by-side groups.

API-MEMBER-b56a77763692.notes: The no-argument form is exact: Geode's activeGroup is only ever a main-area TabGroup, so activeGroup.active is the most recently active root-split leaf. Observed in Electron via the real kanban-bases-view plugin, which uses it to keep the board in front while opening a note behind it. Partial because the optional root argument is typed WorkspaceParent in Obsidian, a WorkspaceItem tree Geode deliberately does not shim; anything other than a Geode TabGroup throws rather than silently searching a wider scope than the caller asked for.

API-MEMBER-38fb23749c97.notes: Added at the Workspace level, where plugins call it: setActiveLeaf previously existed only on TabGroup and Sidebar, and took no options. Both documented forms are accepted, the options object and the deprecated (leaf, pushHistory, focus) triple. focus defaults to false and, when true, moves keyboard focus into the leaf content rather than being accepted and ignored. Observed in Electron restoring the kanban board in front of a note opened behind it.

DEV-3f18652e7e3e.notes: Observed firing on File Explorer right-click for both files and folders, passing the real TAbstractFile (a TFile, or a TFolder as Obsidian does rather than a separate folder-menu event) and the "file-explorer-context-menu" source, with plugin items rendering after the built-ins in the same menu and behind an automatic separator. Fires on a non-markdown file too, where a built-in is withheld but the plugin still receives the TFile. Also now observed firing from the tab-header right-click menu (source "tab-header") and the view-header "more options" ⋮ button (source "more-options"), both passing the optional fourth leaf argument; a tab with no file (e.g. Graph) still shows its built-in menu without firing the event. Remaining gap: Geode has no link/embed context menu at all yet, so the event is not fired from that Obsidian source.

DEV-407dfa8627cb.notes: Observed firing on every editor right-click, including when neither built-in applies, so a plugin can contribute the only item; plugin items append after the built-in Add comment and Bookmark this heading entries when those apply, the menu is suppressed entirely when nothing is added, and Escape dismisses it like any other menu. The second argument is CodeMirror’s EditorView standing in for Obsidian’s Editor wrapper, which Geode does not implement yet, so plugins reading editor methods rather than info.file will not find parity.
